title.zh: 卷二百六十一 列傳第一百四十九 盧象昇 劉之綸 丘民仰
title.en: Volume 261 Biographies 149: Lu Xiangsheng, Liu Zhilun, Qiu Minyang
title.raw: 卷二百六十一 列傳第一百四十九 盧象昇 劉之綸 丘民仰 Volume 261 Biographies 149: Lu Xiangsheng, Liu Zhilun, Qiu Minyang

sentences.zh: 盧象升

translations.literal: Lu Xiangsheng
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangsheng

sentences.zh: 〈（弟象晉象觀從弟象同）〉

translations.literal: (Younger brothers Xiangjin and Xiangguan; cousin Xiangtong.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (His younger brothers were Xiangjin and Xiangguan; his cousin was Xiangtong.)〉

sentences.zh: 劉之綸邱民仰

translations.literal: Liu Zhilun; Qiu Minyang
translations.idiomatic: The biographies treat Liu Zhilun and Qiu Minyang.

sentences.zh: 〈（邱禾嘉）〉

translations.literal: (Qiu Hejia.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Qiu Hejia.)〉

sentences.zh: 盧象升，字建鬥，宜興人。

translations.literal: Lu Xiangsheng, courtesy name Jiandou, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangsheng, whose courtesy name was Jiandou, came from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 祖立誌，儀封知縣。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lizhi was magistrate of Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lizhi had served as magistrate of Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 象升白皙而臞，膊獨骨，負殊力。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng was fair-skinned and lean, with prominent shoulder blades and singular bone structure, yet possessed extraordinary strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng was pale and spare, with striking shoulder blades and an unusual build, yet he possessed remarkable strength.

sentences.zh: 舉天啟二年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Tianqi reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the second year of Tianqi and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 歷員外郎，稍遷大名知府。

translations.literal: He served through the ranks of vice bureau director and was gradually promoted to prefect of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the vice directorships and was eventually promoted to prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，京師戒嚴，募萬人入衛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen, when the capital was placed under martial alert, he recruited ten thousand men to enter the capital on guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongzhen, when Beijing was placed under martial alert, he raised ten thousand men to march to the capital for its defense.

sentences.zh: 明年，進右參政兼副使，整飭大名、廣平、順德三府兵備，號「天雄軍」。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to Right Assistant Commissioner and also served as vice commissioner, taking charge of military preparations in the three prefectures of Daming, Guangping, and Shunde; his force was called the "Tianxiong Army."
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to Right Assistant Commissioner with concurrent duties as vice commissioner, charged with reorganizing the military defenses of Daming, Guangping, and Shunde; his command was styled the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 又明年舉治行卓異，進按察使，治兵如故。

translations.literal: Again the next year, on account of outstanding administrative performance, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner while continuing to command troops as before.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, cited for outstanding governance, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner while continuing to handle military affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 象升雖文士，善射，嫻將略，能治軍。

translations.literal: Although Xiangsheng was a man of letters, he was skilled in archery, well versed in generalship, and able to discipline troops.
translations.idiomatic: Though a scholar by training, Xiangsheng was an able archer, versed in strategy, and skilled at bringing an army under discipline.

sentences.zh: 六年，山西賊流入畿輔，據臨城之西山。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, bandits from Shanxi poured into the capital region and occupied the Western Hills of Lincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, rebels from Shanxi entered the metropolitan region and seized the Western Hills near Lincheng.

sentences.zh: 象升擊卻之，與總兵梁甫、參議寇從化連敗賊。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng drove them back and, together with Regional Commander Liang Fu and Participating Secretary Kou Conghua, inflicted successive defeats on the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng beat them back and, with Regional Commander Liang Fu and Participating Secretary Kou Conghua, defeated them again and again.

sentences.zh: 賊走還西山，圍遊擊董維坤冷水村。

translations.literal: The bandits fled back to the Western Hills and besieged Guerrilla Officer Dong Weikun at Lengshui Village.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels retreated to the Western Hills and besieged Guerrilla Officer Dong Weikun at Lengshui Village.

sentences.zh: 象升設伏石城南，大破之，又破之青龍岡，又破之武安。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng set an ambush south of Shicheng and routed them; he routed them again at Qinglong Ridge and again at Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng laid an ambush south of Shicheng and crushed them; he crushed them again at Qinglong Ridge and yet again at Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 連斬賊魁十一人，殲其黨，收還男女二萬。

translations.literal: In succession he beheaded eleven rebel chiefs, destroyed their bands, and recovered twenty thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: In all he cut down eleven rebel leaders in succession, annihilated their bands, and recovered twenty thousand captives, men and women.

sentences.zh: 三郡之民，安堵者數歲。

translations.literal: For several years the people of the three prefectures lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: For several years thereafter the people of the three prefectures lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 象升每臨陣，身先士卒，與賊格鬥，刃及鞍勿顧，失馬即步戰，逐賊危崖，一賊自巔射中象升額，又一矢仆夫斃馬下，象升提刀戰益疾。

translations.literal: Whenever Xiangsheng took the field he led from the front, grappling with the bandits hand to hand; if a blade reached his saddle he paid no heed, and if he lost his horse he fought on foot, pursuing the enemy up perilous cliffs—once a bandit shot him in the forehead from above, and another arrow felled his groom and horse, yet Xiangsheng seized his blade and fought all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entered battle Xiangsheng placed himself at the head of his men and grappled with the rebels himself; if a blade struck his saddle he ignored it, and if thrown from his horse he fought on foot, chasing them up sheer cliffs—once a rebel on the heights put an arrow in his forehead, and a second arrow killed his groom and horse beneath him, yet Xiangsheng only gripped his saber and fought the harder.

sentences.zh: 賊駭走，相戒曰：「盧廉使遇即死，不可犯。」

translations.literal: The bandits fled in terror, warning one another, "If you meet Vice Commissioner Lu you die—do not provoke him."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled in terror, warning one another, "Meet Vice Commissioner Lu and you die—do not cross him."

sentences.zh: 象昇以是有能兵名。

translations.literal: From this Xiangsheng gained a reputation as a capable commander.
translations.idiomatic: It was thus that Xiangsheng won his name as a commander who could fight.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，南渡河。

translations.literal: The bandits were afraid and crossed the river to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing him, the rebels crossed the Yellow River to the south.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊入楚，陷鄖陽六縣。

translations.literal: The following year the bandits entered Chu, capturing six counties of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the rebels entered Huguang and overran six counties of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 命象升以右僉都御史，代蔣允儀撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace Jiang Yunyi as pacification commissioner of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng was ordered to take up the post of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in place of Jiang Yunyi as pacification commissioner of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 時蜀寇返楚者駐鄖之黃龍灘，象升與總督陳奇瑜分道夾擊，自烏林關、乜家溝、石泉壩、康寧坪、獅子山、太平河、竹木砭、箐口諸處，連戰皆捷，斬馘五千六百有奇，漢南寇幾盡。

translations.literal: At that time Sichuan rebels returning to Chu were encamped at Huanglongtan in Yunyang; Xiangsheng and Governor Chen Qiyu attacked from separate routes in a pincer movement, and from Wulin Pass, Yijia Ravine, Shiquan Dam, Kangning Flat, Lion Mountain, Taiping River, Zhumu Slope, Jingkou, and other places fought successive victorious engagements, beheading more than five thousand six hundred, until the bandits of southern Han were nearly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan rebels who had returned to Huguang were then encamped at Huanglongtan in Yunyang; Xiangsheng and Governor Chen Qiyu struck from separate routes, and from Wulin Pass, Yijia Ravine, Shiquan Dam, Kangning Flat, Lion Mountain, the Taiping River, Zhumu Slope, Jingkou, and other points won battle after battle, slaying more than five thousand six hundred; the rebels of southern Han were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 因請益鄖主兵，減稅賦，繕城郭，貸鄰郡倉谷，募商采銅鑄錢，鄖得完輯。

translations.literal: He therefore requested additional troops for Yunyang, tax reductions, repair of city walls, loans of grain from neighboring prefectural granaries, and recruitment of merchants to mine copper and cast coin; Yunyang was thereby restored to order.
translations.idiomatic: He then petitioned for more regular troops for Yunyang, lighter taxes, repairs to the walls, grain loans from neighboring prefectures, and merchants to mine copper and cast cash; in this way Yunyang was made whole again.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，擢象升右副都御史，代唐暉巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and replaced Tang Hui as governor of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year he was elevated to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and replaced Tang Hui as governor of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 八月，命總理江北、河南、山東、湖廣、四川軍務，兼湖廣巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was ordered to take overall charge of military affairs in Jiangbei, Henan, Shandong, Huguang, and Sichuan, while retaining the governorship of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was charged with overall direction of military affairs in Jiangbei, Henan, Shandong, Huguang, and Sichuan, while continuing as governor of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 總督洪承疇辦西北，象升辦東南。

translations.literal: Governor Hong Chengchou handled the northwest; Xiangsheng handled the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Hong Chengchou was to manage the northwest, Xiangsheng the southeast.

sentences.zh: 尋解巡撫任，進兵部侍郎，加督山西、陜西軍務，賜尚方劍，便宜行事。

translations.literal: Soon he was relieved of the governorship, promoted to Vice Minister of War, and additionally put in charge of military affairs in Shanxi and Shaanxi, with the grant of the imperial sword and discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was relieved of the governorship, promoted to Vice Minister of War, and given additional supervision of Shanxi and Shaanxi military affairs, together with the imperial sword and authority to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 汝、洛告警，象升倍道馳入汝。

translations.literal: When Ruzhou and Luoyang raised the alarm, Xiangsheng forced his march day and night into Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruzhou and Luoyang were threatened, Xiangsheng raced there by forced marches.

sentences.zh: 賊部眾三十余萬，連營百里，勢甚盛。

translations.literal: The rebel host numbered more than three hundred thousand, their encampments stretching a hundred li; their momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel forces numbered more than three hundred thousand, their camps strung out for a hundred li, and their momentum was overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 象升督副將李重鎮、雷時聲等擊高迎祥於城西，用強弩射殺賊千余人。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng directed Vice Generals Li Chongzhen, Lei Shisheng, and others to attack Gao Yingxiang west of the city, using powerful crossbows to kill more than a thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng directed Vice Generals Li Chongzhen, Lei Shisheng, and others to strike Gao Yingxiang west of the city; with heavy crossbows they killed more than a thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 迎祥、李自成走，陷光州，象升復大破之確山。

translations.literal: Yingxiang and Li Zicheng fled; they captured Guangzhou, and Xiangsheng again inflicted a great defeat on them at Queshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang and Li Zicheng withdrew, then took Guangzhou; Xiangsheng again routed them decisively at Queshan.

sentences.zh: 先是，大帥曹文詔、艾萬年陣亡，尤世威敗衄，諸將率畏賊不敢前，象升每慷慨灑泣，激以忠義。

translations.literal: Earlier, the great commanders Cao Wenchao and Ai Wannian had died in battle, You Shiwei had suffered defeat, and the generals for the most part feared the bandits and dared not advance; Xiangsheng would weep freely in indignation and rouse them with appeals to loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the great commanders Cao Wenchao and Ai Wannian had fallen in battle, You Shiwei had been beaten, and most generals were so afraid of the rebels that they would not advance; Xiangsheng would weep openly in his indignation and stir them with talk of loyalty and duty.

sentences.zh: 軍中嘗絕三日餉，象升亦水漿不入口，以是得將士心，戰輒有功。

translations.literal: The army had once gone three days without rations, yet Xiangsheng too took neither food nor drink; in this way he won the hearts of officers and men, and whenever he fought he gained success.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army went three days without pay, yet Xiangsheng likewise took neither food nor drink; by this he won the soldiers' hearts, and in battle he invariably prevailed.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，大會諸將於鳳陽。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he convened the generals at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he assembled the generals at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 象升乃上言曰：「賊橫而後調兵，賊多而後增兵，是為後局；

translations.literal: Xiangsheng then memorialized, saying: "Bandits run rampant and only then are troops mobilized; bandits multiply and only then are reinforcements added—this is fighting from behind;
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng then submitted a memorial, saying, "Rebels grow bold before troops are mobilized; they multiply before reinforcements arrive—this is always fighting from behind;

sentences.zh: 兵至而後議餉，兵集而後請餉，是為危形。

translations.literal: troops arrive and only then is pay discussed; armies gather and only then is pay requested—this is a posture of peril.
translations.idiomatic: pay is debated only after the army arrives; funds are requested only after the host is assembled—this is a posture of extreme danger.

sentences.zh: 況請餉未敷，兵將從賊而為寇，是八年來所請之兵皆賊黨，所用之餉皆盜糧也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when requested funds are not delivered in full, soldiers and officers turn to the bandits and become marauders themselves—in eight years the troops that have been raised have been rebel sympathizers, and the grain that has been spent has been plunderers' provender."
translations.idiomatic: And when the funds requested never fully arrive, officers and men join the rebels and become bandits in their own right—for eight years the soldiers raised have been rebel allies, and the grain spent has been thieves' rations."

sentences.zh: 又言：「總督、總理宜有專兵專餉。

translations.literal: He also said: "The governor and the overall commander ought each to have dedicated troops and dedicated funds.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued, "The governor-general and the overall commander each need troops and funds of their own.

sentences.zh: 請調鹹寧、甘、固之兵屬總督，薊、遼、關、寧之兵屬總理。」

translations.literal: He requested that troops from Xianning, Gansu, and Guyuan be assigned to the governor-general, and troops from Ji, Liaodong, the passes, and Ningxia to the overall commander."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that troops from Xianning, Gansu, and Guyuan be placed under the governor-general, and troops from Ji, Liaodong, the frontier passes, and Ningxia under the overall commander."

sentences.zh: 又言：「各直省撫臣，俱有封疆重任，毋得一有賊警即求援求調。

translations.literal: He also said: "The governors of each province all bear heavy responsibilities for their territories and must not, at the first report of bandits, beg for reinforcements and transfers.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged, "Every provincial governor bears a weighty charge for his territory and must not, at the first alarm of rebels, beg for aid and troop transfers.

sentences.zh: 不應則吳、越也，分應則何以支。」

translations.literal: If no response is made it is like Wu and Yue standing aloof; if responses are divided, how can the realm be sustained?"."
translations.idiomatic: If none respond, it is Wu and Yue standing apart; if all respond piecemeal, how can the state hold?"."

sentences.zh: 又言：「臺諫諸臣，不問難易，不顧死生，專以求全責備。

translations.literal: He also said: "The censorial and remonstrance officials, heedless of difficulty or ease and careless of life or death, devote themselves solely to demanding perfection and assigning blame.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The remonstrance officials, heedless of difficulty or danger and careless of life and death, concern themselves only with demanding perfection and fixing blame.

sentences.zh: 雖有長材，從何展布。

translations.literal: Even men of great talent have no room in which to deploy their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: Even men of real ability have nowhere to show what they can do.

sentences.zh: 臣與督臣，有剿法無堵法，有戰法無守法。」

translations.literal: Your servant and the governor-general have methods for suppression but none for blocking, methods for fighting but none for holding ground."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant and the governor-general have ways to pursue and destroy, but none to block; ways to fight, but none merely to hold ground."

sentences.zh: 言皆切中機宜。

translations.literal: His words all struck at the heart of the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Every point he made went straight to the crux of the matter.

sentences.zh: 於是迎祥圍廬州，不克，分道陷含山、和州，進圍滁州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yingxiang besieged Luzhou without success, split his forces to capture Hanshan and Hezhou, and advanced to besiege Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yingxiang besieged Luzhou without success, sent columns to take Hanshan and Hezhou, and pressed on to besiege Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 象升率總兵祖寬、遊擊羅岱救滁州，大戰城東五里橋，斬賊首搖天動，奪其駿馬。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng led Regional Commander Zu Kuan and Guerrilla Officer Luo Dai to relieve Chuzhou, fought a great battle at Wuli Bridge five li east of the city, beheaded the rebel chief Yaotiandong, and seized his fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng led Regional Commander Zu Kuan and Guerrilla Officer Luo Dai to relieve Chuzhou; east of the city at Wuli Bridge he fought a great battle, slew the rebel chief Yaotiandong, and captured his fine horse.

sentences.zh: 賊連營俱潰，逐北五十里，朱龍橋至關山，積屍填溝委塹，滁水為不流。

translations.literal: The rebel encampments collapsed one after another; pursuing them north fifty li from Zhulong Bridge to Guanshan, corpses filled ditches and ramparts, and the Chu River ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel camps broke entirely; driving them fifty li north from Zhulong Bridge to Guanshan, corpses choked the ditches and ramparts until the Chu River would not flow.

sentences.zh: 賊乃北趨鳳陽，圍壽州，突潁、霍、蕭、碭、靈璧、虹，窺曹、單。

translations.literal: The bandits then turned north toward Fengyang, besieged Shouzhou, burst into Ying, Huo, Xiao, Dang, Lingbi, and Hong, and eyed Cao and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then turned north toward Fengyang, besieged Shouzhou, overran Ying, Huo, Xiao, Dang, Lingbi, and Hong, and threatened Cao and Shan.

sentences.zh: 總兵劉澤清拒河，乃掠考城、儀封而西。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Liu Zeqing blocked them at the river; they therefore plundered Kaocheng and Yifeng and moved west.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Liu Zeqing barred them at the river, so they looted Kaocheng and Yifeng and marched west.

sentences.zh: 其犯亳者，折入歸德。

translations.literal: Those who struck Bo turned inward toward Guide.
translations.idiomatic: The column that struck Bo wheeled into Guide.

sentences.zh: 永寧總兵官祖大樂邀擊之，賊乃北向開封。

translations.literal: Yongning Regional Commander Zu Dale intercepted them, and the bandits then headed north toward Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning Regional Commander Zu Dale intercepted them, and the rebels then turned north toward Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 陳永福敗之朱仙鎮，賊遂走登封，與他賊合，分趨裕州、南陽。

translations.literal: Chen Yongfu defeated them at Zhuxian Town; the bandits fled to Dengfeng, joined other bands, and split toward Yuzhou and Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yongfu routed them at Zhuxian Town; the rebels fled to Dengfeng, merged with other bands, and split toward Yuzhou and Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 象升合寬、大樂、岱兵大破之七頂山，殲自成精騎殆盡。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng combined the forces of Kuan, Dale, and Dai and inflicted a great defeat on them at Qidingshan, nearly annihilating Zicheng's elite cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng united Kuan, Dale, and Dai and crushed them at Qidingshan, nearly wiping out Zicheng's picked horsemen.

sentences.zh: 已，次南陽，令大樂備汝寧，寬備鄧州，而躬率諸軍蹙賊。

translations.literal: Soon after, he halted at Nanyang, ordered Dale to guard Runing, Kuan to guard Dengzhou, and himself led the army to press the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then encamped at Nanyang, set Dale to guard Runing and Kuan to guard Dengzhou, and personally led the armies to hem the rebels in.

sentences.zh: 遣使告湖廣巡撫王夢尹、鄖陽撫治宋祖舜曰：「賊疲矣，東西邀擊，前阻漢江，可一戰殲也。」

translations.literal: He sent messengers to tell Huguang Governor Wang Mengyin and Yunyang Pacification Commissioner Song Zushun: "The bandits are exhausted; strike them from east and west, with the Han River ahead— they can be destroyed in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Huguang Governor Wang Mengyin and Yunyang Commissioner Song Zushun: "The rebels are spent; hit them from east and west with the Han River in front, and they can be wiped out in one fight.

sentences.zh: 兩人竟不能禦，賊遂自光化潛渡漢入鄖。

translations.literal: The two men could not hold them after all; the bandits secretly crossed the Han at Guanghua and entered Yunyang."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two men could not stop them; the rebels slipped across the Han at Guanghua and entered Yunyang."

sentences.zh: 象升遣總兵秦翼明、副將雷時聲由南漳、谷城入山擊賊。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng sent Regional Commander Qin Yiming and Vice General Lei Shisheng through Nanzhang and Gucheng into the mountains to strike the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng dispatched Regional Commander Qin Yiming and Vice General Lei Shisheng through Nanzhang and Gucheng into the hills to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 寬等騎軍，不利阻隘，副將王進忠軍嘩，羅岱、劉肇基兵多逃，追之則彎弓內向。

translations.literal: Kuan's cavalry was ill suited to narrow defiles; Vice General Wang Jinzhong's troops mutinied; Luo Dai's and Liu Zhaoji's soldiers fled in large numbers, and when pursued they turned their bows inward.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's horsemen fared poorly in confined ground; Vice General Wang Jinzhong's men mutinied; many of Luo Dai's and Liu Zhaoji's troops deserted, and when pursued they wheeled about with bows drawn on their own side.

sentences.zh: 象升乃調四川及筸子土兵，搜捕均州賊。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng then transferred Sichuan troops and native soldiers of the Gaozi command to hunt down the bandits of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng then brought up Sichuan troops and Gaozi native levies to hunt the Junzhou rebels.

sentences.zh: 是時，楚、豫賊及迎祥等俱在秦、楚、蜀之交萬山中，象升自南陽趨襄陽進兵。

translations.literal: At this time the bandits of Chu and Henan together with Yingxiang and the rest were all in the myriad mountains where Qin, Chu, and Shu met; Xiangsheng marched from Nanyang toward Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebels of Huguang and Henan, Yingxiang included, were all in the maze of mountains where Shaanxi, Huguang, and Sichuan met; Xiangsheng advanced from Nanyang toward Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 賊多兵少，而河南大饑，餉乏，邊兵益洶洶。

translations.literal: The bandits were many and the troops few; Henan moreover suffered great famine, pay was scarce, and the frontier troops grew ever more unruly.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were plentiful and soldiers few; Henan was in severe famine, funds ran short, and the frontier troops grew increasingly mutinous.

sentences.zh: 承疇、象升議，關中平曠，利騎兵，以寬、重鎮軍入陜，而襄陽、均、宜、谷、上津、南漳，環山皆賊。

translations.literal: Chengchou and Xiangsheng discussed the matter: the Guanzhong plain was open and favored cavalry; Kuan's and Chongzhen's armies should enter Shaanxi, while around Xiangyang, Jun, Yi, Gu, Shangjin, and Nanzhang the mountains on every side harbored bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou and Xiangsheng agreed that the Guanzhong plain, being open, suited cavalry, and that Kuan's and Chongzhen's forces should enter Shaanxi, while Xiangyang, Jun, Yi, Gu, Shangjin, and Nanzhang were ringed by mountains full of rebels.

sentences.zh: 七月，象升渡淅河而南。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Xiangsheng crossed the Xi River and marched south.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Xiangsheng crossed the Xi and marched south.

sentences.zh: 九月，追賊至鄖西。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he pursued the bandits to western Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he pursued the rebels to western Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 京師戒嚴，有詔入衛，再賜尚方劍。

translations.literal: The capital was placed under martial alert and he was ordered to enter on guard duty; the imperial sword was bestowed on him again.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was again placed under alert he was ordered to the capital for its defense, and the imperial sword was granted once more.

sentences.zh: 既行，賊遂大逞，骎驍乎不可復制矣。

translations.literal: Once he had departed, the bandits ran wild and galloped beyond all control.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, the rebels surged unchecked and soon could not be restrained at all.

sentences.zh: 既解嚴，詔遷兵部左侍郎，總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: After the alert was lifted he was ordered transferred to Left Vice Minister of War and made governor-general of Xuan, Datong, and Shanxi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emergency ended he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War and made governor-general of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 大興屯政，谷熟，畝一鐘，積粟二十余萬。

translations.literal: He vigorously promoted garrison farming; grain ripened to one zhong per mu, and more than two hundred thousand dan of grain were stored up.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into garrison agriculture; grain ripened to a full zhong per mu, and more than two hundred thousand dan were stored.

sentences.zh: 天子諭九邊皆式宣、大。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven instructed that all nine frontier commands should take Xuan and Datong as their model.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor directed that all nine frontier districts should follow the Xuan-Datong example.

sentences.zh: 明年春，聞宣警，即夜馳至天城。

translations.literal: The next spring, hearing of an alarm in Xuanfu, he rode through the night to Tiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, on word of trouble in Xuanfu, he galloped through the night to Tiancheng.

sentences.zh: 矢檄旁午，言二百里外乞炭馬蹄闊踏四十里。

translations.literal: Arrows of dispatch flew in from every side, reporting that two hundred li away Qi Tan's horses had trampled a broad track forty li wide.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatches flew in from every quarter, saying that two hundred li away Qi Tan's horses had trampled a track forty li wide.

sentences.zh: 象昇曰：「此大舉也。」

translations.literal: Xiangsheng said: "This is a major incursion."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng said, "This is a major campaign."

sentences.zh: 問：「入口乎？」

translations.literal: He asked: "Have they entered the passes?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "Have they entered the passes?"

translations.literal: The answer was: "Not yet."
translations.idiomatic: The reply was, "Not yet."

sentences.zh: 象升曰：「殆欲右窺雲、晉，令我兵集宣，則彼乘虛入耳。」

translations.literal: Xiangsheng said: "They probably intend to feint toward Yun and Jin on the right, draw our troops to Xuan, and then slip in where we are empty."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng said, "They likely mean to probe Yun and Jin on the right, draw our forces to Xuan, and slip through where we are weak."

sentences.zh: 因檄雲、晉兵勿動，自率師次右衛，戒邊吏毋輕言戰。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered the Yun and Jin troops to hold their positions, led his own army to camp at Youwei, and warned frontier officials not to speak lightly of giving battle.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Yun and Jin armies to stand fast, led his own force to encamp at Youwei, and warned frontier officers not to talk rashly of fighting.

sentences.zh: 持一月，象升曰：「懈矣，可擊。」

translations.literal: After holding for a month Xiangsheng said: "They have grown slack; we can strike.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he said, "They have grown careless; we can strike.

sentences.zh: 哨知三十六營離墻六十里，潛召雲師西來，宣師東來，自督兵直子午，出羊房堡，計日鏖戰。

translations.literal: Scouts reported that the thirty-six camps were sixty li from the wall; he secretly summoned the Yun army from the west and the Xuan army from the east, and himself led troops straight through Ziwu, out by Yangfang Fort, planning to join battle on a set day."
translations.idiomatic: Scouts found the thirty-six camps sixty li from the wall; he secretly called the Yun force from the west and the Xuan force from the east, and personally led his men straight through Ziwu and out by Yangfang Fort to fight on a fixed day."

sentences.zh: 乞炭聞之遂遁。

translations.literal: When Qi Tan heard this he fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Tan heard of it and withdrew immediately.

sentences.zh: 象升在陽和，乞炭不敢近邊。

translations.literal: While Xiangsheng was at Yanghe, Qi Tan did not dare approach the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiangsheng held Yanghe, Qi Tan did not dare come near the border.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁外艱，疏十上，乞奔喪。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he suffered the death of his father; he submitted ten memorials begging leave to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month his father died; he submitted ten memorials begging leave to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 時楊嗣昌奪情任中樞，亦起陳新甲制中，而令象升席喪候代。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Sichang had left mourning to take charge of the central secretariat; Chen Xin Jia was likewise recalled to direct the center, while Xiangsheng was ordered to remain in mourning garb awaiting replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang had meanwhile left mourning to head the Secretariat; Chen Xin Jia was also recalled to the center, while Xiangsheng was left in mourning dress awaiting his successor.

sentences.zh: 進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 新甲在遠，未即至。

translations.literal: Xin Jia was far away and did not arrive promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Jia was still distant and did not arrive at once.

sentences.zh: 九月，大清兵入墻子嶺、青口山，殺總督吳阿衡，毀正關，至營城石匣，駐於牛蘭。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Great Qing army entered through Qiangzi Ridge and Qingkou Mountain, killed Governor Wu Aheng, destroyed the main pass, reached Shixia at Yingcheng, and encamped at Niulan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Qing army entered through Qiangzi Ridge and Qingkou Mountain, killed Governor Wu Aheng, broke the main pass, reached Shixia at Yingcheng, and encamped at Niulan.

sentences.zh: 召宣、大、山西三總兵楊國柱、王樸、虎大威入衛，三賜象升尚方劍，督天下援兵。

translations.literal: The three regional commanders of Xuan, Datong, and Shanxi—Yang Guozhu, Wang Pu, and Hu Dawei—were summoned to the capital on guard duty; the imperial sword was bestowed on Xiangsheng for the third time, and he was put in charge of all relief armies under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The three regional commanders of Xuan, Datong, and Shanxi—Yang Guozhu, Wang Pu, and Hu Dawei—were called to the capital; Xiangsheng received the imperial sword a third time and was placed over all relief armies in the realm.

sentences.zh: 象升麻衣草履，誓師及郊，馳疏報曰：「臣非軍旅才。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng wore hemp and straw sandals, swore in his troops at the suburbs, and sent a hurried memorial reporting: "Your servant is no man of military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Clad in hemp and straw sandals, Xiangsheng took the oath with his army at the city outskirts and sent an urgent memorial: "I am no soldier by talent.

sentences.zh: 愚心任事，誼不避難。

translations.literal: Yet with a simple heart I take on affairs and in duty do not shun hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with an honest heart I accept the charge and in principle do not shrink from hardship.

sentences.zh: 但自臣父奄逝，長途慘傷，潰亂五官，非復昔時；

translations.literal: But since my father's sudden death the long journey has left me shattered in grief, my senses in disorder, no longer what I once was;
translations.idiomatic: But since my father's sudden death the long road has wrecked me with grief; my senses are scattered—I am not the man I was;

sentences.zh: 兼以草土之身踞三軍上，豈惟觀瞻不聳，尤虞金鼓不靈。」

translations.literal: and as one still in the mourning weeds I stand above three armies—not only will the men find the sight unimpressive, I especially fear the drums and gongs will lack power."
translations.idiomatic: and as one still in grave clothes I sit above three armies—not only will the sight fail to inspire awe, I fear above all that drum and gong will lack force."

sentences.zh: 已聞總監中官高起潛亦衰绖臨戎，象升謂所親曰：「吾三人皆不祥之身也。

translations.literal: When he heard that the supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian likewise wore mourning garb as he took the field, Xiangsheng said to those close to him: "We three are all ill-omened men.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian also wore mourning as he went to war, Xiangsheng told those near him, "The three of us are ill-starred men.

sentences.zh: 人臣無親，安有君。

translations.literal: If a minister has no parent, how can he have a lord?
translations.idiomatic: A subject without parents—how can he still have a sovereign?

sentences.zh: 樞輔奪情，亦欲予變禮以分愆耶？

translations.literal: The chief minister has left mourning—does he wish to grant me a change of rites so as to share the blame?
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister has left mourning—does he mean to let me bend ritual so we may share the fault?

sentences.zh: 處心若此，安可與事君。

translations.literal: With a heart disposed in this way, how can one serve the ruler?
translations.idiomatic: A heart set on such things—how can one serve the throne?

sentences.zh: 他日必面責之。」

translations.literal: Another day I shall certainly reproach him to his face."
translations.idiomatic: One day I shall call him to account face to face."

sentences.zh: 當是時，嗣昌、起潛主和議。

translations.literal: At that time Sichang and Qiqian were in charge of peace negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: By then Sichang and Qiqian were steering the court toward peace talks.

sentences.zh: 象升聞之，頓足嘆曰：「予受國恩，恨不得死所，有如萬分一不幸，寧捐軀斷脰耳。」

translations.literal: When Xiangsheng heard of it he stamped his foot and sighed, saying: "I have received the state's grace and only regret that I have no place to die; should there be even one ten-thousandth part of misfortune, I would rather give up my body and sever my neck."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng heard and stamped his foot in anguish: "The state has shown me grace—I only wish I had a place to die. If the slightest mischance should come, I would gladly give my body and let them take my head."

sentences.zh: 及都，帝召對，問方略。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital the emperor summoned him for audience and asked his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he was called in audience and asked for his plan.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣主戰。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Your servant favors fighting."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I favor war."

sentences.zh: 帝色變，良久曰：「撫乃外廷議耳，其出與嗣昌、起潛議。」

translations.literal: The emperor's expression changed; after a long pause he said: "Pacification is only the outer court's discussion—go out and consult with Sichang and Qiqian."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened; after a long silence he said, "Peace is only the outer court's talk—go discuss it with Sichang and Qiqian."

sentences.zh: 出與議，不合。

translations.literal: He went out to consult with them and they did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to meet them and they could not agree.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝發萬金犒軍，嗣昌送之，屏左右，戒毋浪戰，遂別去。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor issued ten thousand in gold to reward the army; Sichang saw him off, dismissed those attending, warned him not to fight recklessly, and then parted.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor sent ten thousand taels in gold to reward the troops; Sichang saw him off, sent attendants away, warned him not to fight rashly, and left.

sentences.zh: 師次昌平，帝復遣中官賫帑金三萬犒軍。

translations.literal: The army halted at Changping; the emperor again sent a eunuch bearing thirty thousand in treasury gold to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped at Changping; the emperor again sent a eunuch with thirty thousand taels from the treasury to reward the men.

sentences.zh: 明日，又賜禦馬百，太仆馬千，銀鐵鞭五百。

translations.literal: The next day he also bestowed a hundred imperial horses, a thousand horses from the Imperial Stud, and five hundred silver-and-iron whips.
translations.idiomatic: The day after he also granted a hundred imperial horses, a thousand from the Imperial Stud, and five hundred silver-tipped iron whips.

sentences.zh: 象升曰：「果然外廷議也，帝意銳甚矣。」

translations.literal: Xiangsheng said: "So it truly was the outer court's discussion—the emperor's own intent is very sharp indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng said, "So it was the outer court after all—the emperor himself is keen for battle.

sentences.zh: 決策議戰，然事多為嗣昌、起潛撓。

translations.literal: He resolved on war, yet affairs were for the most part thwarted by Sichang and Qiqian.
translations.idiomatic: He chose to fight, yet at every turn Sichang and Qiqian obstructed him.

sentences.zh: 疏請分兵，則議宣、大、山西三帥屬象升，關、寧諸路屬起潛。

translations.literal: In a memorial he requested a division of forces; it was decided that the three commanders of Xuan, Datong, and Shanxi should belong to Xiangsheng, while the routes of the passes and Ningxia should belong to Qiqian.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to split the armies: the three Xuan-Datong-Shanxi commanders would answer to Xiangsheng, the frontier passes and Ningxia to Qiqian.

sentences.zh: 象升名督天下兵，實不及二萬。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng was named overseer of all armies under heaven, yet in fact had fewer than twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Though titled commander of all armies in the realm, he had in fact fewer than twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 次順義。

translations.literal: He next encamped at Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his camp to Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 先是，有瞽而賣卜者周元忠，善遼人，時遣之為媾。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been a blind diviner named Zhou Yuanzhong who was skilled with the Liao people and was at times sent to negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a blind fortune-teller, Zhou Yuanzhong, knew the Liao side well and was repeatedly sent to treat for peace.

sentences.zh: 會嗣昌至軍，象升責數之曰：「文弱，子不聞城下盟《春秋》恥之，而日為媾。

translations.literal: When Sichang arrived at the army, Xiangsheng rebuked him, saying: "Wenruo, have you not heard that the Spring and Autumn regards a covenant made beneath the walls as shame—and yet you daily pursue peace?
translations.idiomatic: When Sichang came to camp Xiangsheng upbraided him: "Wenruo, have you not read how the Spring and Autumn counts a treaty under the walls as shame—yet you bargain day after day?

sentences.zh: 長安口舌如鋒，袁崇煥之禍其能免乎？」

translations.literal: The tongues of Chang'an are sharp as blades—can you escape the fate of Yuan Chonghuan?
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an's gossip is sharp as swords—do you think you can escape Yuan Chonghuan's end?

sentences.zh: 嗣昌頰赤，曰：「公直以尚方劍加我矣。」

translations.literal: Sichang's cheeks flushed red and he said: "Sir, you might as well set the imperial sword on my neck."
translations.idiomatic: Sichang flushed and said, "You may as well lay the imperial sword to my throat."

sentences.zh: 象升曰：「既不奔喪，又不能戰，齒劍者我也，安能加人？」

translations.literal: Xiangsheng said: "Having neither left to mourn nor being able to fight, the one who should take the sword in his teeth is myself—how could I lay it on another?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng said, "You would not leave mourning, yet you will not fight—the one who should bite the sword is I. How could I lay it on you?"

sentences.zh: 嗣昌辭遁。

translations.literal: Sichang excused himself and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang made his excuses and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 象升即言：「元忠講款，往來非一日，事始於薊門督監，受成於本兵，通國聞之，誰可諱也？」

translations.literal: Xiangsheng then said: "Yuanzhong's peace talks have gone back and forth for many days; the affair began with the supervising commissioner at Jimen and was concluded by the Minister of War—the whole realm knows it; who can conceal it?
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng went on, "Yuanzhong's negotiations have shuttled back and forth for days; they began with the Jimen supervisor and were sealed by the Minister of War—the whole court knows. Who can hide it?

sentences.zh: 嗣昌語塞而去。

translations.literal: Sichang was left speechless and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang had no reply and left.

sentences.zh: 又數日，會起潛安定門，兩人各持一議。

translations.literal: Several days later he met Qiqian at Anding Gate; the two men each held to one policy.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he met Qiqian at Anding Gate; each clung to his own policy.

sentences.zh: 新甲亦至昌平，象升分兵與之。

translations.literal: Xin Jia also arrived at Changping, and Xiangsheng divided troops and gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Jia reached Changping as well, and Xiangsheng gave him a share of the force.

sentences.zh: 當是時，象升自將馬步軍列營都城之外，沖鋒陷陣，軍律甚整。

translations.literal: At that time Xiangsheng personally led infantry and cavalry arrayed in camps outside the capital, charging in the van; military discipline was very strict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiangsheng himself led foot and horse in camps outside the capital, always in the forefront; his discipline was severe.

sentences.zh: 大清兵南下，三路出師：一由淶水攻易，一由新城攻雄，一由定興攻安肅。

translations.literal: The Great Qing army marched south with three columns: one by Laishui to strike Yi, one by Xincheng to strike Xiong, and one by Dingxing to strike Ansu.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army came south in three columns: one through Laishui against Yi, one through Xincheng against Xiong, one through Dingxing against Ansu.

sentences.zh: 象升遂由涿進據保定，命諸將分道出擊，大戰於慶都。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng then advanced from Zhuo and took position at Baoding, ordering the generals to strike on separate routes; a great battle was fought at Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng advanced from Zhuo to hold Baoding, sent his generals out on separate routes, and fought a great battle at Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 編修楊廷麟上疏言：「南仲在內，李綱無功；

translations.literal: Compiler Yang Tinglin memorialized, saying: "With Nanzhong within and Li Gang ineffective;
translations.idiomatic: Editor Yang Tinglin submitted a memorial: "With Nanzhong inside the palace, Li Gang could achieve nothing;

sentences.zh: 潛善秉成，宗澤殞恨。

translations.literal: with Qianshan holding power, Zong Ze died in regret.
translations.idiomatic: with Qianshan wielding authority, Zong Ze perished in bitterness.

sentences.zh: 國有若人，非封疆福。」

translations.literal: When the state has such men, it is no blessing to the frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the state keeps men like these, the borders are not blessed.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌大怒，改廷麟兵部主事，贊畫行營，奪象升尚書，侍郎視事。

translations.literal: Sichang was furious and transferred Tinglin to a principal clerk in the Ministry of War to assist in the field camp, stripped Xiangsheng of his ministerial title, and had him serve as vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang was enraged, demoted Tinglin to a drafting officer with the field army, reduced Xiangsheng from minister to vice minister, and kept him at work.

sentences.zh: 命大學士劉宇亮輔臣督師，巡撫張其平閉絕餉。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liu Yuliang was ordered as assisting minister to supervise the army; Governor Zhang Qiping cut off supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liu Yuliang was sent to supervise as assisting minister; Governor Zhang Qiping blocked rations.

sentences.zh: 俄又以雲、晉警，趣出關，王樸徑引兵去。

translations.literal: Soon, on alarm from Yun and Jin, he was hurried out of the passes; Wang Pu led his troops away directly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with trouble on the Yun-Jin front, he was pressed to leave the passes; Wang Pu marched his men straight away.

sentences.zh: 象升提殘卒，次宿三宮野外。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng led his battered remnant and encamped in the open country at the Three Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng led his broken remnant and camped in the wilds at the Three Palaces.

sentences.zh: 畿南三郡父老聞之，鹹叩軍門請曰：「天下洶洶且十年，明公出萬死不顧一生之計為天下先。

translations.literal: The elders of the three southern capital districts heard of it and all knocked at the camp gate, pleading: "For ten years the realm has seethed; you, sir, have come forth risking ten thousand deaths and not caring for one life, taking the lead for all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of the three southern districts came to the gate and pleaded: "For ten years the land has boiled in turmoil; you have stepped forward, ready to die ten thousand deaths and not count one life, leading the world.

sentences.zh: 乃奸臣在內，孤忠見嫉。

translations.literal: Yet treacherous ministers are within, and a lone loyal heart is envied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet villains sit within the court, and your solitary loyalty is resented.

sentences.zh: 三軍捧出關之檄，將士懷西歸之心，棲遲絕野，一飽無時。

translations.literal: The three armies wave the order to leave the passes; officers and men cherish thoughts of marching west; they linger in the open wilds without a full meal from day to day.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies flourish the order to march out; soldiers dream of going west; they camp in the wastes and go hungry day after day.

sentences.zh: 脫巾狂噪，雲帥其見告矣。

translations.literal: They throw off their caps and riot; the Yun commander has already sent word.
translations.idiomatic: They tear off their caps and shout; the Yun commander has told us as much.

sentences.zh: 明公誠從愚計，移軍廣順，召集義師。

translations.literal: If you, sir, would truly follow our humble plan, move the army to Guangshun and gather righteous volunteers.
translations.idiomatic: If you would heed our counsel, move to Guangshun and rally loyal volunteers.

sentences.zh: 三郡子弟喜公之來，皆以昔非公死賊，今非公死兵，同心戮力，一呼而裹糧從者可十萬，孰與只臂無援，立而就死哉！」

translations.literal: The young men of the three districts rejoice at your coming; all remember that in the past they would have died for you against bandits, and now would die for you against the invader—if you join hearts and strength, one call and a hundred thousand will wrap grain and follow. How is that worse than standing alone without aid and dying where you stand?
translations.idiomatic: The youths of the three districts rejoice that you have come; they say, 'Before we would have died for you against rebels; now we would die for you against these troops.' Unite in one will and one call will bring a hundred thousand with grain on their backs. How is that worse than standing alone, without help, and dying at once?"

sentences.zh: 象升泫然流涕而謂父老曰：「感父老義。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng wept freely and said to the elders: "I am moved by the elders' righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng wept and told the elders, "Your loyalty moves me.

sentences.zh: 雖然，自予與賊角，經數十百戰未嘗衄。

translations.literal: Yet from the time I matched forces with the bandits I have fought scores and hundreds of battles without defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since I first met the rebels in battle I have fought scores of engagements and never been beaten.

sentences.zh: 今者，分疲卒五千，大敵西沖，援師東隔，事由中制，食盡力窮，旦夕死矣，無徒累爾父老為也。」

translations.literal: Now I have divided out five thousand weary troops; a great enemy presses from the west and relief is cut off to the east; affairs are controlled from the center; food is gone and strength spent—I shall die before long; do not needlessly involve your elders as well."
translations.idiomatic: Now I lead five thousand spent men; a great foe drives from the west and help is blocked to the east; the court meddles from afar; we are out of food and out of strength—I will die soon. Do not let me drag you down with me."

sentences.zh: 眾號泣雷動，各攜床頭鬥粟餉軍，或貽棗一升，曰：「公煮為糧。」

translations.literal: The crowd wailed like thunder; each brought a peck of grain from his bedhead to supply the army, or gave a pint of dates, saying: "Let the lord boil these for his rations."
translations.idiomatic: They cried as one; each brought a peck of grain from home, or a handful of dates, saying, "Boil these for your meal, my lord."

sentences.zh: 十二月十一日，進師至鉅鹿賈莊。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the twelfth month he advanced his army to Jia Village in Julu.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh of the twelfth month he marched to Jia Village in Julu.

sentences.zh: 起潛擁關、寧兵在雞澤，距賈莊五十里而近，象升遣廷麟往乞援，不應。

translations.literal: Qiqian held the Guan-Ning troops at Jize, fifty li from Jia Village and near at hand; Xiangsheng sent Tinglin to beg for reinforcements, but there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqian held the Guan-Ning army at Jize, only fifty li away; Xiangsheng sent Tinglin to beg reinforcements, but none came.

sentences.zh: 師至蒿水橋，遇大清兵。

translations.literal: When the army reached Haoshui Bridge it encountered the Great Qing army.
translations.idiomatic: At Haoshui Bridge the army met the Qing host.

sentences.zh: 象升將中軍，大威帥左，國柱帥右遂戰。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng commanded the center, Dawei the left, and Guozhu the right, and they gave battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng took the center, Dawei the left wing, Guozhu the right, and they joined battle.

sentences.zh: 夜半，觱篥聲四起。

translations.literal: At midnight the sound of suona horns rose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight suona horns sounded from all quarters.

sentences.zh: 旦日，騎數萬環之三匝。

translations.literal: At daybreak tens of thousands of horsemen ringed them three deep.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn tens of thousands of horsemen closed round them in three rings.

sentences.zh: 象升麾兵疾戰，呼聲動天，自辰迄未，炮盡矢窮。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng waved his troops to fight fiercely; the shouts shook heaven; from the hour of chen until wei, cannon were spent and arrows exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng drove his men to fight; the roar shook the sky; from mid-morning until late afternoon powder and arrows were gone.

sentences.zh: 奮身鬥，後騎皆進，手擊殺數十人，身中四矢三刃，遂仆。

translations.literal: He threw himself into the melee; the rear cavalry all pressed forward; with his own hands he killed several dozen men; he took four arrows and three blade wounds and fell.
translations.idiomatic: He plunged into the press; the rear horse all surged up; he cut down dozens with his own hand; four arrows and three blade-cuts struck him, and he fell.

sentences.zh: 掌牧楊陸凱懼眾之殘其屍而伏其上，背負二十四矢以死。

translations.literal: Camp herdsman Yang Lukai, fearing the enemy would mutilate the corpse, lay himself atop it and died with twenty-four arrows in his back.
translations.idiomatic: Herdsman Yang Lukai, fearing the enemy would hack the body, covered it with his own and died with twenty-four arrows in his back.

sentences.zh: 仆顧顯者殉，一軍盡覆。

translations.literal: When he fell, Gu Xian, a man of note, died with him, and the whole army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell, the notable Gu Xian died beside him, and the entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 大威、國柱潰圍乃得脫。

translations.literal: Dawei and Guozhu broke out of the encirclement and only then escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Dawei and Guozhu broke the ring and escaped.

sentences.zh: 起潛聞敗，倉皇遁，不言象升死狀。

translations.literal: When Qiqian heard of the defeat he fled in panic and did not report how Xiangsheng had died.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqian heard of the rout and fled in panic, saying nothing of how Xiangsheng had died.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌疑之，有詔驗視。

translations.literal: Sichang doubted it; an edict was issued to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang doubted the report; the throne ordered the facts checked.

sentences.zh: 廷麟得其屍戰場，麻衣白網巾。

translations.literal: Tinglin recovered his body on the battlefield—he wore hemp garments and a white gauze headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglin found his body on the field—in hemp clothes and a white gauze cap.

sentences.zh: 一卒遙見，即號泣曰：「此吾盧公也。」

translations.literal: A soldier saw him from afar and at once wailed: "This is our Lord Lu.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier glimpsed him from afar and cried, "That is our Lord Lu.

sentences.zh: 三郡之民聞之，哭失聲。

translations.literal: When the people of the three districts heard it they wept until they lost their voices.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the three districts heard and wept until they could not speak.

sentences.zh: 順德知府於穎上狀，嗣昌故靳之，八十日而後殮。

translations.literal: Shunde Prefect Yu Ying submitted a report from Ying; Sichang deliberately withheld it, and burial came only after eighty days.
translations.idiomatic: Shunde Prefect Yu Ying filed a report from the wall; Sichang deliberately held it back, and the burial waited eighty days.

sentences.zh: 明年，象昇妻王請恤。

translations.literal: The next year Xiangsheng's wife Wang requested posthumous favor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xiangsheng's wife Wang petitioned for mourning grants.

sentences.zh: 又明年，其弟象晉、象觀又請，不許。

translations.literal: The year after, his brothers Xiangjin and Xiangguan petitioned again, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Another year on, his brothers Xiangjin and Xiangguan petitioned again, without success.

sentences.zh: 久之，嗣昌敗，廷臣多為言者，乃贈太子少師、兵部尚書，賜祭葬，世蔭錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: After a long while, when Sichang was defeated, many at court spoke on his behalf; only then was he posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, granted funeral rites and burial, and his descendants enfeoffed as a thousand-household hereditary guard of the embroidered guard.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, when Sichang himself was ruined, many at court spoke up; only then was Xiangsheng posthumously made Junior Tutor and Minister of War, given state funeral and burial, and his line enfeoffed as hereditary guard of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 福王時，追謚忠烈，建祠奉祀。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was given the posthumous title Zhonglie and a temple was built for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he received the posthumous name Zhonglie and a shrine was raised for his cult.

sentences.zh: 象升少有大誌，為學不事章句。

translations.literal: In his youth Xiangsheng had great ambitions and in study did not trouble himself with textual glosses.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Xiangsheng harbored great designs and did not fuss over exegetical niceties in his learning.

sentences.zh: 居官勤勞倍下吏，夜刻燭，雞鳴盥櫛，得一機要，披衣起，立行之。

translations.literal: In office he labored twice as hard as his subordinates; at night he burned candles; at cockcrow he washed and combed; whenever he grasped a vital point he rose from bed in his robes and carried it out at once.
translations.idiomatic: In office he worked twice as hard as the men beneath him; he read by candle deep into the night and was washed and combed at cockcrow; the moment he seized a key point he rose in his robes and acted on it.

sentences.zh: 暇即角射，箭銜花，五十步外，發必中。

translations.literal: In leisure he practiced archery; his arrows carried flowers; beyond fifty paces his shots invariably hit.
translations.idiomatic: In spare moments he practiced archery with flowered shafts; fifty paces off, he never missed.

sentences.zh: 愛才惜下如不及，三賜劍，未嘗戮一偏裨。

translations.literal: He loved talent and cherished subordinates as if he could not do enough; though the sword was bestowed three times, he never executed a single junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: He loved able men and cherished his officers beyond measure; though the imperial sword was granted thrice, he never put a single lieutenant to death.

sentences.zh: 高平知縣侯弘文者，奇士也。

translations.literal: Gaoping Magistrate Hou Hongwen was a remarkable man.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Hongwen, magistrate of Gaoping, was a man of unusual spirit.

sentences.zh: 僑寓襄陽，散家財，募滇軍隨象升討賊。

translations.literal: He lodged in Xiangyang, dispersed his family wealth, and recruited Yunnan troops to follow Xiangsheng against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Xiangyang, spent his family fortune, and raised Yunnan troops to follow Xiangsheng against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 象升移宣、大，弘文率募兵至楚，巡撫王夢尹以擾驛聞。

translations.literal: When Xiangsheng moved to Xuan and Datong, Hongwen led his recruits to Chu; Governor Wang Mengyin reported him for disturbing the courier service.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangsheng went to Xuan-Datong, Hongwen brought his recruits to Huguang; Governor Wang Mengyin reported him for harassing the post roads.

sentences.zh: 象升上疏救，不得，弘文卒遣戍。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng memorialized to save him but could not; Hongwen was finally banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng memorialized in his defense but failed; Hongwen was sent to frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 天下由是惜弘文而多象升。

translations.literal: All under heaven therefore pitied Hongwen and admired Xiangsheng the more.
translations.idiomatic: The realm pitied Hongwen and esteemed Xiangsheng all the more.

sentences.zh: 象升好畜駿馬，皆有名字。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng loved to keep fine horses, each with its own name.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng loved fine horses and gave each a name.

sentences.zh: 嘗逐賊南漳，敗，追兵至沙河，水闊數丈，一躍而過，即所號五明驥也。

translations.literal: Once when pursuing bandits at Nanzhang he was defeated; pursuers reached the Sha River, several zhang wide; in one leap he crossed it—this was the steed he called Wuming Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Once, beaten at Nanzhang, pursuers caught him at the Sha River, many zhang across; he cleared it in a single bound—his horse Wuming Ji.

sentences.zh: 方象升之戰歿也，嗣昌遣三邏卒察其死狀。

translations.literal: When Xiangsheng died in battle, Sichang sent three frontier scouts to ascertain how he had perished.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangsheng fell, Sichang sent three frontier scouts to learn how he had died.

sentences.zh: 其一人俞振龍者，歸言象升實死。

translations.literal: One of them, Yu Zhenlong, returned saying Xiangsheng had truly died.
translations.idiomatic: One, Yu Zhenlong, came back reporting that Xiangsheng was truly dead.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌怒，鞭之三日夜，且死，張目曰：「天道神明，無枉忠臣。」

translations.literal: Sichang was enraged and flogged him for three days and nights; as he was near death he opened his eyes and said: "Heaven's way and the spirits are clear—do not wrong a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang flew into a rage and flogged him for three days and nights; near death he opened his eyes and said, "Heaven and the spirits see true—do not wrong a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 於是天下聞之，莫不欷歔，益恚嗣昌矣。

translations.literal: When all under heaven heard of it none could refrain from sighing, and hatred of Sichang grew the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm heard it, none could hold back tears, and men hated Sichang all the more.

sentences.zh: 其後南都亡，象觀赴水死，象晉為僧，一門先後赴難者百余人。

translations.literal: Later, when the Southern Capital fell, Xiangguan threw himself into the water and died; Xiangjin became a monk; more than a hundred of the household in succession met hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Southern Capital was lost, Xiangguan drowned himself; Xiangjin took the tonsure; more than a hundred of the clan died in the calamity.

sentences.zh: 從弟象同及其部將陳安死尤烈。

translations.literal: His cousin Xiangtong and his officer Chen An died especially fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Xiangtong and his officer Chen An died especially hard.

sentences.zh: 象觀，崇禎十五年，鄉薦第一，成進士。

translations.literal: Xiangguan, in the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, placed first in the provincial examination and became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangguan, in Chongzhen 15, topped the provincial exams and took the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 官中書。

translations.literal: He served as a secretary in the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 象晉、象同皆諸生。

translations.literal: Xiangjin and Xiangtong were both licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangjin and Xiangtong were both licentiates.

sentences.zh: 象昇死時，年三十九。

translations.literal: When Xiangsheng died he was thirty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng was thirty-nine when he died.

sentences.zh: 劉之綸，字元誠，宜賓人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhilun, courtesy name Yuancheng, was a native of Yibin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhilun, courtesy name Yuancheng, came from Yibin.

sentences.zh: 家世務農。

translations.literal: His family for generations worked the land.
translations.idiomatic: His family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 之綸少從父兄力田，間艾薪樵，賣之市中。

translations.literal: In his youth Zhilun followed his father and elder brothers in heavy field labor, and between times gathered firewood, which he sold in the market.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zhilun worked the fields beside his father and brothers, and between whiles cut firewood to sell in town.

sentences.zh: 歸而學書，銘其座曰「必為聖人」，里中由是號之綸劉聖人。

translations.literal: Returning home he studied books and inscribed his seat with the words "I must become a sage"; the neighborhood therefore called him Liu the Sage.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he took up books and wrote over his seat, "I must become a sage"; neighbors called him Liu the Sage.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，舉鄉試。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 奢崇明反，以策幹監司扼賊歸路，監司不能用。

translations.literal: When She Chongming rebelled he submitted stratagems to the supervising officials to choke the rebels' line of retreat, but they could not use them.
translations.idiomatic: When She Chongming rose in revolt he offered plans to the supervising officials to cut the rebels' retreat, but they would not adopt them.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年第進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he placed as jinshi and was made a bachelor of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 he took the jinshi and entered the Hanlin as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 與同館金聲及所客申甫三人者相與為友，造單輪火車、偏廂車、獸車，刳木為西洋大小炮，不費司農錢。

translations.literal: Together with his colleague Jin Sheng and his guest Shen Fu the three became friends and devised a single-wheeled fire cart, a side-carriage cart, and a beast cart; they hollowed wood into Western-style great and small cannon without spending Ministry of Revenue funds.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended his Hanlin colleague Jin Sheng and a guest, Shen Fu; together they built a single-wheeled fire cart, a side-carriage, and a beast-drawn cart, and hollowed logs into large and small Western-style cannon without drawing on the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: The next winter the capital was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter the capital was placed under martial alert.

sentences.zh: 聲上書得召見，薦之綸及甫。

translations.literal: Sheng submitted a memorial and was summoned for audience; he recommended Zhilun and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Sheng memorialized and was called to audience; he recommended Zhilun and Fu.

sentences.zh: 帝立召之綸、甫。

translations.literal: The emperor at once summoned Zhilun and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately summoned Zhilun and Fu.

sentences.zh: 之綸言兵，了了口辨。

translations.literal: When Zhilun spoke of military affairs his exposition was perfectly clear and his eloquence sharp.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhilun spoke of war his exposition was lucid and his tongue quick.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，授甫京營副總兵，資之金十七萬召募；

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and appointed Fu vice regional commander of the Capital Garrison, supplying him with one hundred seventy thousand in funds for recruitment;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and made Fu vice commander of the Capital Garrison, funding him with 170,000 taels to raise troops;

sentences.zh: 改聲御史，監其軍；

translations.literal: Sheng was changed to censor and supervised his army;
translations.idiomatic: Jin Sheng was made a censor to oversee the force;

sentences.zh: 授之綸兵部右侍郎，副尚書閔夢得協理京營戎政。

translations.literal: Zhilun was made Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of War; Vice Minister Min Mengde assisted in managing the capital garrison's military administration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilun was appointed Right Vice Minister of War; Vice Minister Min Mengde helped coordinate capital garrison affairs.

sentences.zh: 於是之綸賓賓以新進驟躋卿貳矣。

translations.literal: Thus Zhilun, a newly advanced man, had in short order leapt to a second-rank ministerial post.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhilun, still a newcomer, had vaulted to a vice-ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 初，正月元日有黑氣起東北亙西方。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the first day of the first month, a black vapor rose in the northeast and stretched across to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on New Year's Day, black vapor had risen in the northeast and stretched westward.

sentences.zh: 甫見之大驚，趨語之綸、聲曰：「天變如此，汝知之乎？

translations.literal: When Fu saw it he was greatly alarmed and hurried to tell Zhilun and Sheng: "Heaven's change is like this—do you know it?
translations.idiomatic: Fu was deeply alarmed and rushed to Zhilun and Sheng: "Heaven shows such a sign—do you understand it?

sentences.zh: 今年當喋血京城下，可畏也。」

translations.literal: This year blood will be shed beneath the capital walls—it is fearful.
translations.idiomatic: This year blood will run under the capital walls. It is terrifying.

sentences.zh: 聞者皆笑。

translations.literal: Those who heard all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who heard them laughed.

sentences.zh: 及冬十一月三日，大清兵破遵化，十五日至壩上，二十日薄都城，自北而西。

translations.literal: By winter, on the third day of the eleventh month, the Great Qing army broke Zunhua; on the fifteenth it reached Bashang; on the twentieth it pressed the capital from the north and west.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the third of the eleventh month, the Qing took Zunhua; on the fifteenth they reached Bashang; on the twentieth they pressed the capital from the north and west.

sentences.zh: 都人從城上望之，如雲萬許片馳風，須臾已過。

translations.literal: People in the capital looked from the walls and saw them like ten thousand sheets of cloud driven by the wind; in an instant they had passed.
translations.idiomatic: From the walls the people saw them like ten thousand clouds driven by wind; in a moment they had swept past.

sentences.zh: 遂克良鄉，還至蘆溝，夜殺甫一軍七千余人，黎明掩殺大帥滿桂、孫祖壽，生擒黑雲龍、麻登雲以去。

translations.literal: They then took Liangxiang and returned to Lugou; that night they killed more than seven thousand of Fu's army; at dawn they ambushed and killed the great commanders Man Gui and Sun Shou, and took Heiyunlong and Ma Dengyun alive.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Liangxiang, withdrew to Lugou, killed more than seven thousand of Fu's men that night, and at dawn ambushed the great commanders Man Gui and Sun Shou, taking Heiyunlong and Ma Dengyun alive.

sentences.zh: 之綸曰：「元日之言驗矣。」

translations.literal: Zhilun said: "The words of New Year's Day have been verified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilun said, "What we said on New Year's Day has come true.

sentences.zh: 請行，無兵，則請京營兵，不許；

translations.literal: He requested to take the field; without troops he asked for capital-garrison troops—not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: He asked to march; without troops he begged for capital-garrison soldiers—refused;

sentences.zh: 則請關外川兵，不許；

translations.literal: then he asked for Sichuan troops from beyond the passes—not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: then for frontier Sichuan troops—refused;

sentences.zh: 則議召募，召募得萬人，遂行。

translations.literal: then they discussed recruitment; when recruitment yielded ten thousand men, he set out.
translations.idiomatic: then for a levy; when ten thousand were raised, he marched.

sentences.zh: 抵通州，時永平已陷，天大雨雪。

translations.literal: Reaching Tongzhou, Yongping had already fallen; heaven sent great rain and snow.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongzhou, Yongping had already fallen; rain and snow fell in torrents.

sentences.zh: 之綸奏軍機，七上，不報。

translations.literal: Zhilun memorialized on military affairs seven times; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilun sent seven military memorials; none was answered.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，師次薊。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the army halted at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the new year his army encamped at Ji.

sentences.zh: 當是時，大清兵蒙古諸部號十余萬，駐永平；

translations.literal: At that time the Great Qing army and the Mongol tribes together numbered more than a hundred thousand and were encamped at Yongping;
translations.idiomatic: The Qing host and Mongol allies numbered more than a hundred thousand at Yongping;

sentences.zh: 諸勤王軍數萬在薊。

translations.literal: the various relief armies numbered tens of thousands at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: relief armies in the tens of thousands lay at Ji.

sentences.zh: 之綸乃與總兵馬世龍、吳自勉約，由薊趨永平，牽之無動，而自率兵八路進攻遵化。

translations.literal: Zhilun then agreed with Regional Commanders Ma Shilong and Wu Zimian to hurry from Ji toward Yongping and hold the enemy in place without moving, while he himself led his troops in eight columns to attack Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilun agreed with Ma Shilong and Wu Zimian to rush from Ji toward Yongping and pin the enemy, while he led eight columns against Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 既由石門至白草頂，距遵化八里娘娘山而營，世龍、自勉不赴約。

translations.literal: Having passed through Shimen to Baicao Peak, he encamped eight li from Zunhua at Niangniang Mountain; Shilong and Zimian did not keep the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He marched through Shimen to Baicao Peak and camped eight li from Zunhua at Niangniang Mountain; Shilong and Zimian never came.

sentences.zh: 二十二日，大清兵自永平趨三屯營，驍騎三萬，望見山上軍，縱擊之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second the Great Qing army hurried from Yongping toward Santunying; thirty thousand elite horsemen saw the troops on the mountain and charged them.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second the Qing force hurried from Yongping toward Santunying; thirty thousand picked horsemen saw the hilltop army and charged.

sentences.zh: 之綸發炮，炮炸，軍營自亂。

translations.literal: Zhilun fired his cannon; the cannon burst and the camp fell into disorder of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilun fired his guns; a piece burst and his camp collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 左右請結陣徐退，以為後圖，之綸叱曰：「毋多言！

translations.literal: Those beside him asked to form ranks and withdraw slowly for a later plan; Zhilun rebuked them: "Say no more!
translations.idiomatic: His officers begged to form up and withdraw for another day; Zhilun snapped, "Enough talk!

sentences.zh: 吾受國恩，吾死耳！」

translations.literal: I have received the state's grace—I die, that is all!
translations.idiomatic: I owe the state my life—that is all there is to it!

sentences.zh: 嚴鼓再戰，流矢四集。

translations.literal: He beat the drums fiercely and fought again; stray arrows flew in from every side.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the drums for another stand; arrows flew from every side.

sentences.zh: 之綸解所佩印付家人，「持此歸報天子」，遂死。

translations.literal: Zhilun took the seal from his belt and gave it to a family member: "Take this back and report to the Son of Heaven," and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilun handed his seal to a kinsman: "Take this to the Son of Heaven," and died.

sentences.zh: 一軍皆哭，拔營野戰，皆死之。

translations.literal: The whole army wept, broke camp for field battle, and all died.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army wept, left camp to fight in the open, and perished to a man.

sentences.zh: 屍還，矢飲於顱，不可拔，聲以齒嚙之出，以授其家人。

translations.literal: When the body was returned, an arrow had drunk into the skull and could not be drawn; Sheng bit it out with his teeth and gave it to the family.
translations.idiomatic: When the body came back, an arrow had sunk into the skull and would not come free; Sheng bit it out with his teeth and gave it to the kin.

sentences.zh: 初，講官文震孟入都，之綸、聲往見之，震孟教以持重。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lecturer Wen Zhenmeng entered the capital, Zhilun and Sheng went to see him; Zhenmeng taught them to be steady and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lecturer Wen Zhenmeng had entered the capital; Zhilun and Sheng visited him, and he taught them to be steady.

sentences.zh: 之綸既受命視師，驟貴，廷臣抑之。

translations.literal: Once Zhilun had received command of the army and suddenly risen high, court officials held him down.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhilun took command and rose so fast, the courtiers checked him.

sentences.zh: 震孟使人諷之，謂宜辭侍郎而易科銜以行，不聽。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng sent word advising him to resign the vice-ministerial title and take a lower bureau rank on campaign; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng hinted he should drop the vice-ministership and march under a lesser title; he refused.

sentences.zh: 既行，通州守者不納，雨雪宿古廟中，御史董羽宸劾其行留。

translations.literal: After he marched, the Tongzhou garrison would not admit him; in rain and snow he lodged in an old temple; Censor Dong Yuchen impeached him for lingering on the march.
translations.idiomatic: On the march Tongzhou would not let him in; he slept in a ruined temple in snow; Censor Dong Yuchen accused him of delay.

sentences.zh: 之綸曰：「小人意忌，有事則委卸，無事則議論，止從一侍郎起見耳。

translations.literal: Zhilun said: "Petty men are jealous; when there is work they shirk it, when there is none they talk—this is only because they look at one vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilun said, "Small men envy me; they shirk work and chatter when there is none—all because I am a vice minister.

sentences.zh: 乞削臣今官，賜骸骨。」

translations.literal: I beg that my present office be stripped and my bones sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Strip my rank and let me go home in my bones.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: It was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 及戰死，天子嘉其忠，從優恤，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When he died in battle the Son of Heaven praised his loyalty and granted favorable mourning; he was posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell the emperor praised his loyalty and granted generous mourning, posthumously making him Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 震孟止之曰：「死綏，分也，侍郎非不尊。」

translations.literal: Zhenmeng stopped it, saying: "To die holding one's post is one's portion; a vice minister is not lacking in honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng objected: "Dying at one's post is duty enough; a vice minister is honor enough.

sentences.zh: 遂不予贈，賜一祭半葬，任一子。

translations.literal: Posthumous promotion was therefore not granted; half a funeral sacrifice was given and one son was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: So the higher posthumous rank was denied; he received half the state rites and one son was enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 之綸母老，二子幼，貧不能返柩，請於朝，給驛還。

translations.literal: Zhilun's mother was old and his two sons young; they were too poor to return the coffin and petitioned the court, which gave them courier stations for the journey home.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was old, his sons young; too poor to bring the coffin home, they petitioned and were given post relays.

sentences.zh: 久之，贈尚書。

translations.literal: After a long while he was posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was posthumously made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 後十五年，聲死難。

translations.literal: Fifteen years later Sheng also died in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later Jin Sheng too died in the nation's ruin.

sentences.zh: 邱民仰，字長白，渭南人。

translations.literal: Qiu Minyang, courtesy name Changbai, was a native of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Minyang, courtesy name Changbai, came from Weinan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 以教諭遷順天東安知縣，厘宿弊十二事。

translations.literal: As an instructor he was transferred to magistrate of Dong'an in Shuntian and cleared twelve longstanding abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from instructor to magistrate of Dong'an in Shuntian, he swept away twelve entrenched abuses.

sentences.zh: 河嚙，歲旱蝗，為文祭禱。

translations.literal: The river gnawed the banks; drought and locusts came in the same year; he wrote ritual texts and prayed.
translations.idiomatic: The river ate its banks; drought and locusts struck together; he wrote prayers and offered sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 河他徙，蝗亦盡。

translations.literal: The river shifted elsewhere and the locusts vanished as well.
translations.idiomatic: The river shifted course and the locusts vanished.

sentences.zh: 調繁保定之新城。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the demanding post of Xincheng in Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the demanding county of Xincheng in Baoding.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，縣被兵，晨夕登陴守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen the county suffered military attack; morning and evening he mounted the walls to defend.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 the county was harried by troops; dawn to dusk he manned the walls.

sentences.zh: 四方勤王軍畢出其地，民仰調度有方，民不知擾。

translations.literal: Relief armies from all quarters passed through his territory; Minyang coordinated them so skillfully that the people scarcely felt disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Armies hurrying to the capital all passed through; Minyang directed them so well the people barely noticed.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，號敢言。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor and was known for daring speech.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to censor and was famed for blunt speech.

sentences.zh: 時四方多盜，鎮撫率怯懦不敢戰，釀成大亂。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were numerous in every quarter; pacification commissioners were for the most part cowardly and dared not fight, brewing great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed everywhere; pacifiers were timid and would not fight, brewing catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 吳橋兵變，列城多陷，巡撫余大成、孫元化皆主撫。

translations.literal: When the Wuqiao mutiny broke out many cities fell; Governors Yu Dacheng and Sun Yuanhua both favored appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuqiao mutiny toppled many towns; Governors Yu Dacheng and Sun Yuanhua both favored negotiation.

sentences.zh: 流賊擾山西，巡撫宋統殷下令，殺賊者抵死。

translations.literal: When roving bandits harried Shanxi, Governor Song Tongyin ordered that killing bandits would be punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels ravaged Shanxi, Governor Song Tongyin decreed death for anyone who killed a "bandit."

sentences.zh: 民仰先後疏論其非，後皆如民仰言。

translations.literal: Minyang memorialized repeatedly that this was wrong, and later events proved him right.
translations.idiomatic: Minyang protested again and again; events later proved him right.

sentences.zh: 遭妻喪，告歸。

translations.literal: When his wife died he asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After his wife's death he sought leave to mourn at home.

sentences.zh: 出為河間知府，遷天津副使，調大同監軍汝寧，遷永平右參政，移督寧前兵備。
