translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Hejian, was moved to vice commissioner at Tianjin, transferred to supervise troops at Runing in Datong, promoted to Right Assistant Commissioner at Yongping, and shifted to supervise Ningqian military preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Hejian, vice commissioner at Tianjin, military supervisor at Runing in Datong, Right Assistant Commissioner at Yongping, and finally Ningqian military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 民仰善理劇，以故所移皆要地。

translations.literal: Minyang was skilled at handling heavy affairs, and for that reason every post he held was a key one.
translations.idiomatic: Minyang excelled at knotty administration, so every post he held was critical.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，擢右僉都御史，代方一藻巡撫遼東，按行關外八城，駐寧遠。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace Fang Yizao as governor of Liaodong; he inspected the eight cities beyond the pass and stationed at Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 13 he became Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, replacing Fang Yizao as Liaodong governor; he toured the eight outer cities and camped at Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 十四年春，錦州被圍，填壕毀塹，聲援斷絕。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year Jinzhou was besieged; moats were filled and ramparts destroyed; communications were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 14 Jinzhou was besieged; ditches filled, walls ruined, links severed.

sentences.zh: 有傳其帥祖大壽語者：「逼以車營，毋輕戰。」

translations.literal: There was a report in the words of its commander Zu Dashou: "They are pressing us with wagon forts—do not fight lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Word came in Zu Dashou's name: "They press us with wagon forts—do not fight rashly.

sentences.zh: 總督洪承疇集兵，民仰轉餉，未發。

translations.literal: Governor-General Hong Chengchou gathered troops; Minyang was turning supplies but had not yet dispatched them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Hong Chengchou massed the army; Minyang was forwarding grain but had not yet sent it.

sentences.zh: 帝憂之。

translations.literal: The emperor was worried.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 朝議兩端。

translations.literal: Court debate wavered between two policies.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion was divided.

sentences.zh: 命郎中張若麒就行營計議，若麒至，則趣進師。

translations.literal: Bureau Director Zhang Ruoji was ordered to the camp to deliberate; when Ruoji arrived he urged an advance.
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhang Ruoji was sent to camp to decide; on arrival he pressed for battle.

sentences.zh: 七月，師次乳峰，去錦州五六里而營，旦日，楊國柱之軍潰。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the army halted at Rufeng, encamped five or six li from Jinzhou; the next day Yang Guozhu's army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the host camped at Rufeng, five or six li from Jinzhou; next day Yang Guozhu's wing broke.

sentences.zh: 逾月，王樸軍亦潰。

translations.literal: After more than a month Wang Pu's army also collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: A month on, Wang Pu's force collapsed too.

sentences.zh: 未幾，馬科等五將皆潰。

translations.literal: Before long the five generals Ma Ke and the rest all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ma Ke and four other generals were routed as well.

sentences.zh: 大清兵掘松山，斷我歸路，遂大敗，蹂躪殺溺無算，退保松山。

translations.literal: The Great Qing army dug at Songshan and cut our line of retreat; there was a great defeat with trampling, killing, and drowning beyond counting; the army fell back to hold Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing dug at Songshan and severed retreat; the rout was beyond counting—trampled, slain, drowned; the army clung to Songshan.

sentences.zh: 圍急，外援不至，芻糧竭。

translations.literal: The siege was desperate, outside aid did not come, and fodder and grain were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege tightened, no relief came, grain and fodder ran out.

sentences.zh: 至明年二月，且半年矣，城破，承疇降，民仰死，若麒跳從海上蕩漁舟而還，寧遠、關門勁旅盡喪。

translations.literal: By the second month of the next year, nearly half a year having passed, the city fell; Chengchou surrendered; Minyang died; Ruoji fled by leaping onto a fishing boat at sea and returned; Ningyuan and the passes lost their crack troops entirely.
translations.idiomatic: By the second month of the next year—nearly half a year—the city fell; Chengchou surrendered; Minyang died; Ruoji escaped by fishing boat; Ningyuan and the passes lost their best troops.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝驚悼甚，設壇都城，承疇十六，民仰六，賜祭盡哀。

translations.literal: When word came the emperor was deeply shocked and grieved; altars were set in the capital—sixteen for Chengchou, six for Minyang—with sacrifices and full mourning.
translations.idiomatic: News reached the capital; the emperor was stricken; altars rose in the city—sixteen rites for Chengchou, six for Minyang—with full mourning.

sentences.zh: 贈民仰右副都御史，官為營葬，錄其一子。

translations.literal: Minyang was posthumously made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; the state arranged his burial and enfeoffed one son.
translations.idiomatic: Minyang was posthumously Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; the state buried him and enfeoffed a son.

sentences.zh: 尋命建祠都城外，與承疇並列，帝將親臨祭焉。

translations.literal: Soon orders went out to build a shrine outside the capital wall, standing with Chengchou's; the emperor was to attend in person.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine outside the walls was ordered, paired with Chengchou's; the emperor would worship in person.

sentences.zh: 將祭，聞承疇降，乃止。

translations.literal: As the rites were about to begin, word came that Chengchou had surrendered, and they were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When worship was due, news came that Chengchou had surrendered, and the rites were canceled.

sentences.zh: 邱禾嘉，貴州新添衛人。

translations.literal: Qiu Hejia was a native of Xintian Guard in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Hejia came from Xintian Guard in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷四十一年鄉試，好談兵。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the forty-first year of Wanli and loved to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial exams in Wanli 41 and loved to talk of war.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，安邦彥反，捐資制器，協擒其黨何中蔚。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign, when An Bangyan rebelled, he donated funds to make weapons and helped capture his partisan He Zhongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi, when An Bangyan rebelled, he funded arms and helped seize the rebel He Zhongwei.

sentences.zh: 選祁門教諭，以貴州巡撫蔡復一請，遷翰林待詔，參復一軍。

translations.literal: Selected as instructor of Qimen, at the request of Guizhou Governor Cai Fuyi he was moved to Hanlin attendant and joined Fuyi's army.
translations.idiomatic: Made instructor at Qimen, then—at Governor Cai Fuyi's request—Hanlin attendant on Fuyi's staff.

sentences.zh: 寧遠自畢自肅遇害，遂廢巡撫官，以經略兼之，至是議復設。

translations.literal: After Bi Zisu was killed at Ningyuan the governorship was abolished and the frontier commissioner took charge; now it was debated whether to restore it.
translations.idiomatic: After Bi Zisu's death at Ningyuan the Liaodong governorship was dropped and the frontier commissioner took over; now restoration was debated.

sentences.zh: 廷棟力推禾嘉才，超拜右僉都御史，巡撫其地，兼轄山海關諸處。

translations.literal: Tingdong strongly pushed Hejia's talent; he was abruptly made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to govern the region and also oversee Shanhaiguan and other points.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong pushed Hejia's talent; he was suddenly made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief for the region, also overseeing Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 禾嘉初蒞鎮，大清兵以二萬騎圍錦州，禾嘉督諸將赴救，城獲全。

translations.literal: When Hejia first took command, the Great Qing army with twenty thousand horsemen besieged Jinzhou; Hejia directed the generals to the relief and the city was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: On taking command the Qing invested Jinzhou with twenty thousand horse; Hejia led relief and saved the city.

sentences.zh: 登萊巡撫孫元化議徹島上兵於關外，規復廣寧及金、海、蓋三衛，禾嘉議用島兵復廣寧、義州、右屯。

translations.literal: Deng-Lai Governor Sun Yuanhua proposed withdrawing island troops to the outer passes to recover Guangning and the three guards of Jin, Hai, and Gai; Hejia proposed using island troops to recover Guangning, Yizhou, and Youtun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuanhua of Deng-Lai wanted island troops beyond the passes to retake Guangning and the Jin-Hai-Gai guards; Hejia wanted them for Guangning, Yizhou, and Youtun.

sentences.zh: 廷棟慮其難，以咨承宗。

translations.literal: Tingdong feared the difficulty and consulted Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong doubted the plan and asked Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 承宗上奏曰：「廣寧去海百八十里，去河百六十里，陸運難。

translations.literal: Chengzong memorialized: "Guangning is one hundred eighty li from the sea and one hundred sixty li from the river—transport by land is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong wrote: "Guangning lies 180 li from the sea and 160 li from the river—land supply is hard.

sentences.zh: 義州地偏，去廣寧遠，必先據右屯，聚兵積粟，乃可漸逼廣寧。」

translations.literal: Yizhou lies off to the side, far from Guangning; one must first hold Youtun, gather troops and grain, and only then gradually press toward Guangning."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou is remote from Guangning; hold Youtun first, mass grain and men, then edge toward Guangning."

sentences.zh: 又言：「右屯城已隳，修築而後可守。

translations.literal: He also said: "The wall at Youtun is already ruined; it must be rebuilt before it can be held.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Youtun's wall is broken—it must be rebuilt to be held.

sentences.zh: 築之，敵必至，必復大、小淩河，以接松、杏、錦州。

translations.literal: If it is built, the enemy will certainly come; they will certainly retake the Greater and Lesser Ling Rivers to link Songshan, Xingzhou, and Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuild it and the enemy will come—they will retake the Greater and Lesser Ling to link Songshan, Xing, and Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 錦州繞海而居敵，難陸運。

translations.literal: Jinzhou sits wrapped by the sea among enemies—overland supply is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou hugs the sea amid foes—land routes are hard.

sentences.zh: 而右屯之後即海，據此則糧可給，兵可聚，始得為發軔地。」

translations.literal: But behind Youtun lies the sea; hold this place and grain can be brought, troops gathered—only then is there a starting point."
translations.idiomatic: Behind Youtun is the sea; hold it and grain and troops can flow—only then is there a foothold."

sentences.zh: 奏入，廷棟力主之，於是有大淩築城之議。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Tingdong strongly backed it, and thus arose the plan to build the Greater Ling fortress."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial entered; Tingdong backed it hard, and the Greater Ling fort was born."

sentences.zh: 會禾嘉訐祖大壽，大壽亦發其贓私。

translations.literal: Then Hejia impeached Zu Dashou and Dashou in turn exposed his graft.
translations.idiomatic: Hejia denounced Zu Dashou; Dashou exposed his corruption.

sentences.zh: 承宗不欲以武將去文臣，抑使弗奏，密聞於朝，請改禾嘉他職。

translations.literal: Chengzong did not wish to remove a military man because of a civil official and suppressed the report, secretly informing the court and asking that Hejia be transferred to another post.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong would not see a general removed by a civil officer; he suppressed the papers, secretly asked the court to move Hejia.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，命調南京太仆卿，以孫谷代。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was ordered transferred to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing; Sun Gu was to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 4 he was ordered to Nanjing as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud; Sun Gu would replace him.

sentences.zh: 谷未至，部檄促城甚急。

translations.literal: Gu had not yet arrived when urgent orders from the ministry pressed construction of the fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had not arrived when the ministry urgently pressed fort building.

sentences.zh: 大壽以兵四千據其地，發班軍萬四千人築之，護以石矽土兵萬人。

translations.literal: Dashou held the ground with four thousand troops; fourteen thousand rotating troops were sent to build it, guarded by ten thousand Shixi native soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou held the site with four thousand men; fourteen thousand rotating laborers built, guarded by ten thousand Shixi natives.

sentences.zh: 禾嘉往視之，條九議以上。

translations.literal: Hejia went to inspect it and submitted nine proposals upward.
translations.idiomatic: Hejia inspected the works and submitted nine proposals.

sentences.zh: 工垂成，廷棟罷去。

translations.literal: The work was nearly finished when Tingdong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The works were nearly done when Tingdong fell from power.

sentences.zh: 廷議大淩荒遠不當城，撤班軍赴薊，責撫鎮矯舉，令回奏。

translations.literal: Court debate held that Greater Ling was too remote and should not be fortified; rotating troops were withdrawn to Ji; the pacification commissioner was blamed for reckless recommendation and ordered to report back.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Greater Ling too remote to fortify; rotating troops were pulled to Ji; the governor was rebuked for reckless counsel and told to answer.

sentences.zh: 禾嘉懼，盡撤防兵，留班軍萬人，輸糧萬石濟之。

translations.literal: Hejia was afraid and withdrew all defensive troops, leaving ten thousand rotating troops and sending ten thousand dan of grain to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing censure, Hejia pulled back the garrison, left ten thousand rotating troops, and sent ten thousand dan of grain.

sentences.zh: 八月，大清兵抵城下，掘濠築墻，四面合圍，別遣一軍截錦州大道。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Great Qing army reached beneath the walls, dug moats and built ramparts, surrounded on four sides, and sent a separate force to cut the Jinzhou road.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Qing came under the walls, dug trenches, built parapets, invested on four sides, and detached a force to sever the Jinzhou road.

sentences.zh: 城外堠臺皆下，城中兵出，悉敗還。

translations.literal: The beacon towers outside the walls were all taken down; troops sallied from the city and were all beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: Outer beacon towers fell; sorties from the city were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 禾嘉聞之，馳入錦州，與總兵官吳襄、宋偉合兵赴救。

translations.literal: When Hejia heard of it he hurried into Jinzhou and, with Regional Commander Wu Xiang and Song Wei, combined forces to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Hejia raced into Jinzhou and joined Wu Xiang and Song Wei for relief.

sentences.zh: 離松山三十餘里，與大清兵遇，大戰長山、小淩河間，互有傷損。

translations.literal: Thirty-odd li from Songshan they met the Great Qing army and fought a great battle between the Long and Lesser Ling Rivers, each side suffering damage.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li from Songshan they met the Qing and fought hard between the Long and Lesser Ling, both sides taking losses.

sentences.zh: 九月望，大清兵薄錦州，分五隊直抵城下。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth of the ninth month the Great Qing army pressed Jinzhou and in five columns came straight to the walls.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the ninth month the Qing pressed Jinzhou in five columns to the walls.

sentences.zh: 襄、偉出戰不勝，乃入城。

translations.literal: Xiang and Wei went out to fight without success and then entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang and Wei sallied, failed, and withdrew into the city.

sentences.zh: 二十四日，監軍張春會襄、偉兵，過小淩河東五里，築壘列車營，為大淩聲援。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth Supervising Commissioner Zhang Chun joined Xiang and Wei's troops, crossed five li east of the Lesser Ling River, built ramparts and arrayed wagon forts, as a relief force for Greater Ling.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth Commissioner Zhang Chun joined Xiang and Wei, crossed five li east of the Lesser Ling, built ramparts and wagon forts to support Greater Ling.

sentences.zh: 大清兵扼長山，不得進。

translations.literal: The Great Qing army held Long Mountain and they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing held Long Mountain and they could not get through.

sentences.zh: 禾嘉遣副將張洪謨、祖大壽、靳國臣、孟道等出戰五里莊，亦不勝。

translations.literal: Hejia sent Vice Generals Zhang Hongmo, Zu Dashou, Jin Guochen, Meng Dao, and others to fight at Wulizhuang and again they did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Hejia sent Zhang Hongmo, Zu Dashou, Jin Guochen, Meng Dao, and others to Wulizhuang; again they lost.

sentences.zh: 夜趨小淩河，至長山接戰，大敗。

translations.literal: At night they hurried to the Lesser Ling River; reaching Long Mountain they joined battle and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At night they rushed to the Lesser Ling; at Long Mountain they fought and were shattered.

sentences.zh: 春及副將洪謨、楊華征、薛大湖等三十三人俱被執，副將張吉甫、滿庫、王之敬等戰歿。

translations.literal: Chun and Vice Generals Hongmo, Yang Huazheng, Xue Dahu, and thirty others were all captured; Vice Generals Zhang Jifu, Manku, Wang Zhijing, and others died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, Hongmo, Yang Huazheng, Xue Dahu, and thirty others were taken; Zhang Jifu, Manku, Wang Zhijing, and others fell.

sentences.zh: 大壽不敢出，淩城援自此絕。

translations.literal: Dashou dared not come out, and relief to the Ling fortress was cut off from this point.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou would not sally forth; from then on Greater Ling had no relief.

sentences.zh: 敗書聞，舉朝震駭。

translations.literal: When word of defeat came the whole court was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: News of the rout shook the court.

sentences.zh: 孫谷代禾嘉，未至而罷，改命謝璉。

translations.literal: Sun Gu was to replace Hejia but had not arrived when the appointment was canceled; Xie Lian was appointed instead.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gu was named to replace Hejia but never came; Xie Lian was appointed.

sentences.zh: 璉畏懼，久不至。

translations.literal: Lian was afraid and for a long time did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was timid and long delayed.

sentences.zh: 後兵事亟，召璉駐關外，禾嘉留治中。

translations.literal: Later, as military affairs grew urgent, Lian was summoned to station beyond the pass while Hejia remained to administer the interior.
translations.idiomatic: As war pressed on, Lian was called to the frontier while Hejia stayed inland.

sentences.zh: 及是聞敗，移駐松山，圖再舉，言官以推委詆之帝。

translations.literal: On hearing of the defeat he moved his station to Songshan intending to try again; remonstrance officials accused him of shirking before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the rout he shifted to Songshan to try again; censors accused him of evasion.

sentences.zh: 帝以禾嘉獨守松山，非卸責，戒飭而已。

translations.literal: The emperor held that Hejia alone held Songshan and was not shirking responsibility; he was only admonished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Hejia was holding Songshan, not shirking, and merely warned him.

sentences.zh: 大淩糧盡食人馬。

translations.literal: At Greater Ling grain was gone and men ate horses.
translations.idiomatic: At Greater Ling grain ran out and men ate their horses.

sentences.zh: 大清屢移書招之，大壽許諾，獨副將可綱不從。

translations.literal: The Great Qing repeatedly sent letters summoning surrender; Dashou agreed, but only Vice General Ke Gang refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing sent repeated summons; Dashou agreed; only Vice General Ke Gang refused.

sentences.zh: 十月二十七日，大壽殺可綱，與副將張存仁等三十九人投誓書約降。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month Dashou killed Ke Gang and, with Vice General Zhang Cunren and thirty-eight others, submitted a sworn pact to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh of the tenth month Dashou killed Ke Gang; with Zhang Cunren and thirty-eight others he swore surrender.

sentences.zh: 是夕出見，以妻子在錦州，請設計誘降錦州守將，而留諸子於大清。

translations.literal: That evening he went out to an audience, saying that because his wife and children were in Jinzhou he asked to devise a plan to lure the Jinzhou garrison to surrender while leaving his sons with the Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: That night he appeared, pleading that with wife and children in Jinzhou he would lure the garrison while leaving his sons as hostages.

sentences.zh: 禾嘉聞大淩城炮聲，謂大壽得脫，與襄及中官李明臣、高起潛發兵往迎。

translations.literal: When Hejia heard cannon from Greater Ling he thought Dashou had broken out and, with Xiang and the eunuchs Li Mingchen and Gao Qiqian, sent troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing guns at Greater Ling, Hejia thought Dashou had broken out and with Xiang and eunuchs Li Mingchen and Gao Qiqian sent troops to meet him.

sentences.zh: 適大壽偽逃還，遂俱入錦州。

translations.literal: Just as Dashou pretended to flee back, they all entered Jinzhou together.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou feigned escape and they all entered Jinzhou together.

sentences.zh: 大淩城人民商旅三萬有奇，僅存三之一，悉為大清所有，城亦被毀。

translations.literal: The people, travelers, and merchants of Greater Ling numbered more than thirty thousand; only a third survived; all the rest became possessions of the Great Qing, and the fortress was destroyed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Ling held more than thirty thousand people and travelers; only a third lived; the rest went to the Qing and the fort was razed.

sentences.zh: 十一月六日，大清復攻杏山，明日攻中左所。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the eleventh month the Great Qing again attacked Xingshan; the next day they attacked Zhongzuosuo.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth of the eleventh month the Qing struck Xingshan; next day Zhongzuosuo.

sentences.zh: 城上用炮擊，乃退。

translations.literal: The city answered with cannon fire and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cannon from the walls drove them back.

sentences.zh: 大壽入錦州，未得間，而禾嘉知其納款狀，具疏聞於朝。

translations.literal: Dashou entered Jinzhou but had not yet found an opening; Hejia learned of his surrender and submitted a full report to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou entered Jinzhou without an opening; Hejia learned he had surrendered and reported fully.

sentences.zh: 因初奏大壽突圍出，前後不讎，引罪請死。

translations.literal: Because his first report said Dashou had broken out of the encirclement, the two accounts did not agree; he confessed guilt and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: His first report said Dashou had broken out—now the stories clashed; he confessed and begged death.

sentences.zh: 於是言官交劾，嚴旨飭禾嘉。

translations.literal: Thereupon remonstrance officials impeached him in succession and stern orders rebuked Hejia.
translations.idiomatic: Censors piled on; stern edicts rebuked Hejia.

sentences.zh: 而帝於大壽欲羈縻之，弗罪也。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor wished to keep Dashou on a leash and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor meant to keep Dashou on a string and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 新撫璉已至，禾嘉猶在錦州，會廷議山海別設巡撫。

translations.literal: The new governor Lian had arrived, yet Hejia was still at Jinzhou; the court debated setting a separate governor for Shanhai.
translations.idiomatic: New governor Lian had come, but Hejia remained at Jinzhou; the court debated a separate Shanhai governor.

sentences.zh: 詔罷璉，令方一藻撫寧遠，禾嘉仍以僉都御史巡撫山海、永平。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Lian and ordered Fang Yizao to govern Ningyuan; Hejia remained Vice Censor-in-Chief governing Shanhai and Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was dismissed; Fang Yizao took Ningyuan; Hejia kept his rank over Shanhai and Yongping.

sentences.zh: 尋論築城召釁罪，貶二秩，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was judged guilty of provoking war by building the fortress, demoted two ranks, but kept the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was found guilty of provoking war by building the fort, demoted two ranks, but kept office.

sentences.zh: 禾嘉請為監視中官設標兵。

translations.literal: Hejia requested that a picked force be set up for the supervising eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Hejia asked for an elite guard for the supervising eunuch.

sentences.zh: 御史宋賢詆其諂附中人，帝怒，貶賢三秩。

translations.literal: Censor Song Xian accused him of flattering the inner court; the emperor was angry and demoted Xian three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Song Xian called it flattery of the eunuchs; the emperor was angry and demoted Xian three ranks.

sentences.zh: 禾嘉持論每與承宗異，不為所喜，時有詆諆。

translations.literal: Hejia's views often differed from Chengzong's and were not to his liking; there was constant slander.
translations.idiomatic: Hejia often disagreed with Chengzong, who disliked him; slander followed.

sentences.zh: 既遭喪敗，廷論益不容，遂堅以疾請。

translations.literal: After these defeats court opinion would no longer tolerate him, and he firmly pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: After the disasters the court would not bear him; he pleaded illness in earnest.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，詔許還京，以楊嗣昌代。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year an edict allowed him to return to the capital; Yang Sichang was to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 5 he was allowed back to the capital; Yang Sichang would replace him.

sentences.zh: 令其妻代陳病狀。

translations.literal: He had his wife submit a report of illness on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: His wife filed illness on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 乃命歸田，未出都卒。

translations.literal: He was ordered to retire to his fields but died before leaving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered home to his fields, he died before he left the capital.

sentences.zh: 明世舉於鄉而仕至巡撫者，隆慶朝止海瑞，萬歷朝張守中、艾穆。

translations.literal: In the Ming, those who passed the provincial examination and rose to governor—in the Longqing reign only Hai Rui; in the Wanli reign Zhang Shouzhong and Ai Mu.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming times, provincials who rose to governor: under Longqing only Hai Rui; under Wanli Zhang Shouzhong and Ai Mu.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝破格求才，得十人：邱民仰、宋一鶴、何騰蛟、張亮以忠義著，劉可訓以武功聞，劉應遇、孫元化、徐起元皆以勤勞致位，而陳新甲官最顯。

translations.literal: The Chongzhen emperor broke precedent to seek talent and found ten: Qiu Minyang, Song Yihe, He Tengjiao, and Zhang Liang were noted for loyalty and righteousness; Liu Kexun for military achievement; Liu Yingyu, Sun Yuanhua, and Xu Qiyuan for labor reaching high office; Chen Xin Jia rose highest of all.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen broke form to find talent and got ten: Minyang, Song Yihe, He Tengjiao, and Zhang Liang for loyalty; Liu Kexun for arms; Liu Yingyu, Sun Yuanhua, and Xu Qiyuan for tireless service; Chen Xin Jia rose highest.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：危亂之世，未嘗乏才，顧往往不盡其用。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In ages of peril talent is never lacking, yet it often is not fully used.
translations.idiomatic: The comment says: In dangerous times talent is never scarce, yet it is seldom fully used.

sentences.zh: 用矣，或掣其肘而驅之必死。

translations.literal: When it is used, someone often seizes its elbow and drives it to certain death.
translations.idiomatic: When used, someone often holds its arm and drives it to die.

sentences.zh: 若是者，人實為之，要之亦天意也。

translations.literal: When this happens, men have done it—but in the end it is also Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: Men do this—but in the end Heaven wills it too.

sentences.zh: 盧象升在莊烈帝時，豈非不世之才，乃困抑之以至死，何耶！

translations.literal: Was not Lu Xiangsheng in the time of Chongzhen a talent of his age—yet he was pressed down until death; why!
translations.idiomatic: Was not Lu Xiangsheng under Chongzhen a man of his age—yet crushed to death; why!

sentences.zh: 至忠義激發，危不顧身，若劉之綸、邱民仰之徒，又相與俱盡，則天意可知矣。

translations.literal: When loyalty and righteousness are roused and men do not flinch from peril, as with Liu Zhilun, Qiu Minyang, and their kind, all perishing together—then Heaven's will may be known.
translations.idiomatic: When loyalty and duty stir men to face death unflinching, as with Liu Zhilun, Qiu Minyang, and such, all falling together—then Heaven's intent is plain.
